metadata.case_name: SIU SIU KING v. WONG CHAK WING

plaintiff.occupation_before: part-time secretary for Madam Chow Mei Ling; sales lady for a health food company

source: According to the medical report from Eastern Hospital dated 21 January 2004, the Plaintiff complained of left knee injury in the accident on admission.
I found that the Plaintiff only suffered knee injury, contusion to neck and back in the accident.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the knee or lower leg, unspecified

source: I found that the Plaintiff only suffered knee injury, contusion to neck and back in the accident.
At the accident, the Plaintiff suffered whiplash injury to her waist and back.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of neck

source: She also suffered mild adjustment disorder that does not affect her working ability.
Dr. Chung opined that the Plaintiff is suffering from adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood.

manifestations.description: numbness radiating to the upper limbs and right lower limb
jerky limb movements / seizure-like non-epileptic attacks
bed bound / reported inability to walk

treatments_received: admission to Eastern Hospital (initial treatment and discharge same day)
admission to St. Paul's Hospital (10 July 2000 to 14 July 2000)
physiotherapy (Eastern Hospital from 3 August 2000 to 28 December 2000)
clinical psychology / psychologist treatment (3 sessions at Eastern Hospital)
bonesetters' treatment (10 sessions in Hong Kong)
admission to Queen Mary Hospital (18 September 2003)
transfer to Fung Yiu King Hospital for rehabilitation (from 7 October 2003)
treatments_future: psychiatric treatment (5 sessions recommended by Dr. Chung)

losses.description: Pain and suffering from whiplash/contusion to neck and back and knee injury resulting from the accident
She also suffered mild adjustment disorder that does not affect her working ability. Dr. Chung opined that the Plaintiff is suffering from adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood.
